terms.comment: A description of ours: grānum, a grain or seed, and versicolor, of many colours (Cicero of feathers, plūmae versicolōrēs, Fin. 3.18, Lewis & Short). We have found no word for sprinkles in Traupman, Morgan–Owens, or Levi–Bini. Cato strewed poppy seed over his honeyed cakes, papāver īnfriātō (Cato Agr. 79, 84); to scatter sprinkles, aspergere (see “sprinkle”).

phrases.latin: Grāna saccharī versicolōria super placentam asperge.
phrases.english: Scatter the sprinkles over the cake.

phrases.latin: coctōs eximitō, eōs melle unguitō, papāver īnfriātō, ita pōnitō
phrases.english: take them out when they are done, brush them with honey, sprinkle poppy seed over them, and serve

sources: Lewis & Short: granum · Lewis & Short: versicolor · Lewis & Short: infrio · Lewis & Short: papaver
